speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the exact location of your sudden abdominal pain and what you were doing when it started. To help me assess the severity, have you experienced any nausea, vomiting, or changes in bowel movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Mesenteric Ischemia. The sudden onset of pain around the umbilicus in a 74-year-old with recent acute myocardial infarction, followed by bloody stools, is highly suggestive of bowel ischemia due to embolic or thrombotic occlusion. Immediate surgical consultation and imaging are critical. REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Angiography_Abdomen_Pelvis.
